foregroundStars.basis: Milky Way foreground stars by the criterion of Ren et al. (2021, Sect. 3.2): a Gaia parallax measured to better than 20% that places the star within 50 kpc (parallax above 0.02 mas), or a proper motion in right ascension or declination above 0.2 mas/yr plus 2 sigma, measured to better than 20%. Applied to Gaia DR3 within 2.3 deg of M31's centre, which covers the photograph's crop; the query is in the Gaia DR3 source record. Laid on M31's 77.5 deg disc, each of these round stars becomes a dash 4.6 times longer than it is wide.

companions.basis: M32 and NGC 205 are separate galaxies near M31 on the sky; laid on M31's disc with the rest of the photograph, each becomes a bright streak. Their centres and half-light ellipses are the Local Volume Database's (structure from McConnachie 2012); how far each glow reaches is measured in the image. Andromeda IX, the third companion in the field, does not show in it.

colourTie.basis: RC3 (de Vaucouleurs et al. 1991, CDS VII/155) gives NGC 224 a total (B-V)T of 0.92 +/- 0.02 as observed from Earth, through the Milky Way; corrected for Galactic and internal extinction it is 0.68 ((B-V)oT). The composite's own colour comes from its publisher's UBVI and H-alpha mapping, which runs red; red and blue are scaled in linear light so the disc's mean colour matches the engine's catalogue colour for B-V 0.92, the function that colours the star dots.

survey.credit: Local Group Survey Team and T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage)

fill.credit: ESA/Hubble & Digitized Sky Survey 2. Acknowledgment: Davide De Martin (ESA/Hubble)

composition.basis: The survey panorama is about three times sharper than the DSS2 view and in true UBVI and H-alpha colour, but it is a strip 55 arcmin wide whose notches reach 11.8 kpc into the disc; the DSS2 view fills them and the outer disc, its light histogram-matched to the survey's over the pixels both cover. The frame runs along the survey's strip at 2 arcsec per pixel. The 2 arcmin fade and the no-data level are presentation choices.
